citation: Decker et al. 2024. Body Positions and Physical Activity Levels Modulate the Ratio of Abdominal to Thoracic Breathing and Respiratory Rate in Young Individuals. Journal of Clinical Medicine
protocol: Respiratory belts at rest in standing, sitting, supine and prone; two groups by physical activity (low and high)
population: 37 young adults aged 21 +/- 2 y in low and high physical-activity groups
note: Each posture printed as mean and SD per activity group, so posture is stated. Rest only, no exercise. Abstract says 'young individuals'; health status as printed is not 'healthy' in the abstract, but no disease is listed.
